author: mvanhorn
body:
The published `ordertogo` CLI was broken at three layers and could not complete any API call against ordertogo.com. This PR fixes all three.

### What was broken

1. **Chrome cookie decryption on macOS.** `third_party/kooky/browser/chrome/chrome.go` selected the `value` column (deprecated, always empty on macOS) instead of `encrypted_value`, and had no decryption path. `auth login --chrome` silently imported zero cookies. A separate `chromeTime` bug overflowed int64 nanoseconds for any far-future expiry and wrapped every cookie's `Expires` to year 1442, which `kooky.Valid` then rejected.
2. **Server auth gate.** ordertogo.com returns `403 Access denied` for every `/m/api/*` request that lacks a browser-shaped `User-Agent` plus `Origin` and `Referer`. The CLI sent `ordertogo-pp-cli/0.1.0` with neither, so every command failed even with a valid cookie session.
3. **Wrong checkout endpoint and processor.** Generated `orders place` drove a headless Chrome through a Braintree DropIn flow against UI selectors that do not exist on the live site. The actual checkout endpoint is `POST /m/api/postmicmeshorder` and payment is Stripe with a saved customer + card key, captured directly from a real `$2.99` browser checkout.

### Fix

1. `third_party/kooky/browser/chrome/chrome.go` snapshots the Cookies DB (to avoid Chrome's exclusive lock), reads `encrypted_value`, derives an AES-128 key from `security find-generic-password -wa Chrome` via PBKDF2 (`saltysalt`, 1003 iters), AES-CBC-decrypts v10/v11, strips PKCS#7 padding, and strips the 32-byte `SHA-256(host_key)` prefix Chrome M120+ prepends for v10 host-binding. `chromeTime` now goes through `time.Unix` to avoid the overflow.
2. `internal/client/client.go` defaults `User-Agent` to a Mozilla string and sets `Origin` + `Referer` from `c.BaseURL` when the caller did not override.
3. `internal/cli/orders_place.go` was rewritten to call `POST /m/api/postmicmeshorder` directly with the Stripe-saved-card body. Cart comes from a localStorage-shape JSON file (`--cart-file`) or the existing active cart (`--reuse-last`). Payment IDs land in config via new keys (`stripe_customer_id`, `stripe_default_card`, `customer_firstname`, `customer_lastname`, `customer_phone`). The `--max` budget gate stays in front of the POST.

### Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go build ./...` | PASS |
| `go vet ./...` | PASS |
| `go test ./...` | PASS (92 tests / 11 packages) |
| `govulncheck ./...` | PASS (no vulnerabilities) |
| `verify_skill.py --dir library/food-and-dining/ordertogo/` | PASS |
| `auth login --chrome` (live macOS Chrome) | 8 cookies imported (was 0) |
| `restaurants menu --slug mixsushibarlin` (live API) | 200 OK (was 403) |
| `PRINTING_PRESS_VERIFY=1 orders place --cart-file ... --confirm` | body byte-for-byte identical to a real successful `$2.99` browser checkout |

### Patches manifest

Added a second entry to `.printing-press-patches.json` (`ordertogo-fix-broken-auth-and-checkout`) covering the four touched files; every changed site carries a `// PATCH:` comment per repo convention.

## Зачем

ASI-вердикт по PR-14 пометил H5: поле formula_project_types.engine_modules читалось только GET /api/v3/project-types для UI и не влияло на работу пайплайна. Оркестратор гейтил стадии только через skip_* флаги.

## Было / Стало

Было: PipelineOrchestrator выполнял стадии intake/demand/crawl/audit/preflight/pack, пропуская их только по skip_demand/skip_crawl и hasUrl. engine_modules из БД оркестратор не читал.

Стало: перед запуском оркестратор читает engine_modules для project_code из formula_project_types (либо принимает override через PipelineInput.engine_modules для тестов и DI). Стадии, отсутствующие в whitelist, помечаются как skipped с reason engine_modules_disabled и не выполняются. Существующие skip_* флаги сохранены как user override.

## Логика гейтинга

Приоритет: engine_modules whitelist выше, чем skip_*. Если стадия отсутствует в whitelist — это engine_modules_disabled, даже когда юзер выставил skip-флаг. Если стадия в whitelist, но юзер выставил skip — это user_skip_flag.

Решения собираются в PipelineResultV3.decision_trace заранее, до try{} c buildStrategy/passport, чтобы трасса оставалась полной даже при падении промежуточной стадии.

Маппинг стадия оркестратора → модуль в БД:
- intake → intake
- demand → demand
- crawl → crawl
- audit → audit
- preflight → preflight
- pack → developerPack

- owndev-backend/src/services/pipeline/pipelineOrchestrator.ts: helper loadEngineModulesFromDb, STAGE_TO_MODULE маппинг, pre-compute decision_trace, гейтинг 6 стадий.

- owndev-backend/src/services/pipeline/__tests__/pr19-engine-modules-whitelist.ts: unit-тест с whitelist [preflight, demand] и skip_demand=true — проверяет, что 4 стадии помечены engine_modules_disabled, demand — user_skip_flag, preflight — enabled.
- owndev-backend/package.json: новый script test:pr19-engine-modules, включён в test:bridge.

- /geo-audit, /geo-rating, geo_* — не менялось.

- Миграции БД — не менялись.

## Summary

- Implemented MPPI and Smooth MPPI for cartpole swing-up.
- Added PyTorch controller implementations.
- Added JAX controller implementations using `vmap`, `lax.scan`, and `jit`.
- Added benchmark and result summary under `results/tables/benchmark_results.md`.

## Results

- Cartpole initial condition: Pole hanging straight down, cartpole motionless
- MPPI success/failure: Succeeds consistently. 
- Smooth MPPI success/failure: Succeeds consistently. 
- Best PyTorch MPPI runtime: 0.016 s
- Best PyTorch Smooth MPPI runtime: 0.016 s
- Best JAX MPPI runtime: 0.009 s
- Best JAX Smooth MPPI runtime: 0.010 s
- Hardware used: M4 Max (JAX using CPU, PyTorch using GPU). We found that JAX performed best on CPU while PyTorch performed best on GPU. We chose to compare the best runtime performances of both.

## Tuning Notes

- Horizon length: 70 timesteps
- Number of samples: 20,000
- Temperature / lambda: 1
- Noise covariance: 3 for MPPI, 0.7 for SMPPI
- Control limits: $-10\ N \le u \le 10\ N$
- Cost terms: $\theta^2 + x^2 + 1000C$ where $x$ is the cart's distance from the center and $C$ is an indicator function whose value is 1 if constraints are violated.
- Smoothness penalty or smoothing strategy: None for MPPI, $0.01\cdot \Delta u^2$ for SMPPI


## Answers

### What are the pros and cons of MPPI compared with Smooth MPPI?
MPPI produces noisy control outputs, which may be infeasible or dangerous for an actuator to actually perform. MPPI implementations address this by adding a smoothing step after the controls are calculated using an algorithm like SGF. This approach has certain limitations, such as introducing control constraint violations or system response delay. SMPPI addresses this by sampling derivatives, but it may perform worse compared to MPPI when discontinuous control outputs are optimal.

### What are the pros and cons of sampling-based MPC compared with nonlinear MPC using nonlinear solvers?
Sampling-based MPC can be highly efficient since each trajectory rollout can be explored in parallel. It also allows for discontinuities and nonconvexities in the cost function that nonlinear solvers would struggle with. However, its sampling-based nature can result in noise and chattering in the control output.

Nonlinear MPC using nonlinear solvers is better at enforcing constraints and produces smooth solution trajectories. However, it requires that the system's dynamics are given so that a gradient can be computed. 

### What are the runtime differences between the PyTorch and JAX implementations?
The JAX implementations are faster than their PyTorch counterparts. There was an initial runtime cost for JAX's JIT compilation, but we found that JAX's runtime was faster on subsequent calls.

### When would you prefer PyTorch for this controller, and when would you prefer JAX?
JAX consistently ran faster than the PyTorch implementations. We would prefer JAX for its runtime advantage, but we are less comfortable working in JAX. PyTorch may be preferred for prototyping and experimentation, but JAX is preferred for the final implementation.

body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: User passwords were being hashed with a simple SHA-256 algorithm without any salt. This made the stored credentials vulnerable to rainbow table attacks if the local storage (`SharedPreferences`) were ever compromised or extracted.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could easily reverse-engineer weak or common passwords by looking up the hash in a precomputed rainbow table, leading to unauthorized account access.
🔧 Fix: Updated `LocalAuthService` to generate a secure random 16-byte salt using `dart:math`'s `Random.secure()`. This salt is appended to the password before hashing, and stored alongside the hashed password in the credentials JSON. During sign-in, the stored salt is used to verify the password. Backward compatibility is maintained for old unsalted accounts by defaulting to an empty string if the salt key is missing.
✅ Verification: `flutter test test/services/local_auth_service_test.dart` passes. New tests specifically assert that a salt is stored, and that two identical passwords for different users result in entirely different hashes.

**`api()` helper envelope:**
- Unwraps `subsonic-response` on `status=ok`.

Summary: Implement Multi-Coin Backend Support for Address Page
This PR transforms the address page backend from a single-coin (VAR-only) model to a multi-coin model (VAR + SKA{n}), as specified in the implementation plan. It enables the explorer to track, calculate, and serve balance and transaction data for multiple coin types per address while maintaining strict precision for SKA atoms.
Key Changes
1. Core Data Structures (db/dbtypes)
- Multi-Coin Balance: Replaced flat balance fields in AddressBalance with a Coins map[uint8]*CoinBalance.
- CoinBalance Struct: Introduced CoinBalance to handle the dual-nature of assets (int64 atoms for VAR, string atoms for SKA).
- Chart Data Extension: Extended ChartsData to support server-side cumulative balances for SKA (BalanceAtoms, etc.), ensuring the frontend never performs BigInt arithmetic.
- Address Info: Added ActiveCoins to AddressInfo to identify all coin types present at a specific address.
2. Query Layer & Logic (db/dcrpg)
- Coin-Aware Queries: Implemented retrieveAddressCoinTypes and updated retrieveAddressBalance to preserve the coin-type dimension.
- Server-Side Cumsum: Implemented running balance calculations in Go using *big.Int for SKA atoms to prevent precision loss.
- Stake Metrics Fix: Updated stake income/spending ratios to be computed exclusively from VAR coin balances, as stake is VAR-denom uma.
- Coin Filtering: Modified AddressData and TxHistoryData to support the ?coin=N filter, defaulting to the first member of ActiveCoins.
3. Mempool & Helpers
- Coin-Aware Mempool: Updated UnconfirmedTxnsForAddress to return transaction counts per coin type.
- Tx Metadata: Extended TxWithBlockData and PrevOut to carry CoinType and SKAValue throughout the pipeline.
4. API & Explorer Handlers
- Chart API: Added ?coin=N filtering to chart endpoints.
- CSV Exports: Extended CSV logic to include coin_type and output SKA amounts as strings.
- XHR Parity: Ensured AddressTable XHR refreshes respect the same coin filtering as the initial SSR.
- Fiat Removal: Removed all fiat conversion logic (FiatBalance) as no coins in the network currently have a reliable market price.
5. Caching & Performance
- Coin-Aware Cache: Updated AddressCache to store per-coin balance maps and chart series.
- Filtered Caching: Chart data is now cached per-coin to ensure efficient retrieval of filtered views.
6. Backward Compatibility (Hotfix)
- Added temporary mock fields to AddressBalance and AddressPageData to prevent template execution failures (TotalUnspent, FiatBalance, etc.) until the frontend templates are updated.
Verification Results
- Unit Tests: New tests for CoinBalance JSON marshaling and ActiveCoins sorting.
- Integration Tests: Verified AddressData and TxHistoryData with mixed-coin addresses.
- API Tests: Validated ?coin=N filtering and default coin fallback behavior.
- Build: Verified that the dcrdata binary builds without errors.

body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `drafter_eligible_friendly_names: list[str]` field on
`ModelCard` and resolves it against the live `state.node_identities` map
at placement time. Resolved IDs are merged (deduped, raw-first) with the
existing `drafter_eligible_nodes: list[NodeId]` field before
`_select_drafter_placement` runs.

## Why

Raw NodeIds are 32-char libp2p peer IDs derived from a node's persistent
keypair (e.g. `12D3KooWBehfQMu654A6RcG7zbYTg4JBajzXi8nupKs5NgjwGMsu`).
They survive normal reboots and re-elections, but regenerate if the
operator wipes the keypair (`rm -rf ~/.exo`). For our asymmetric drafter
override TOMLs, this means:

- The override is **deploy-specific** — every operator workstation gets
  a different NodeId for the same physical node, so the same TOML can't
  be reused across machines.
- After any state wipe, the pin goes stale and asymmetric drafter
  silently degrades (the rank is just not appended) until the operator
  re-edits the TOML with the new ID.

The asymmetric drafter feature explicitly requires `drafter_eligible_nodes`
to be non-empty (see `_select_drafter_placement` in `placement.py:604`),
so we can't just drop the pin. The fix is to let the operator name the
eligible nodes by the same friendly hostname (`wc-bmbp`, etc.) the info
gatherer already publishes into `node_identities`.

## What changed

- `src/exo/shared/models/model_cards.py` — adds
  `drafter_eligible_friendly_names: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)`
  alongside the existing `drafter_eligible_nodes` field. Both fields can
  be set on the same card; the resolver dedupes.
- `src/exo/master/placement.py` — new public helper
  `resolve_drafter_eligible_nodes(model_card, node_identities)` that
  returns the merged, deduped, order-preserved list. `place_instance`
  gains a `node_identities` keyword (defaulting to `None`) and threads
  the resolved list into `_select_drafter_placement` via a new
  `resolved_eligible_nodes` keyword.
- `src/exo/master/main.py` — passes `self.state.node_identities` from
  the command-handling site to `place_instance`.
- `src/exo/master/tests/test_placement_drafter_friendly_names.py` — 8 new
  tests covering legacy passthrough, friendly-name resolution, dedup
  across both fields, unmatched name silently dropped,
  `node_identities=None` skip path, ordering, and one full end-to-end
  `place_instance` flow.

## Backward compat

- `drafter_eligible_friendly_names` defaults to empty list. Existing
  TOMLs with only `drafter_eligible_nodes` populated work byte-for-byte.
- The `node_identities` parameter on `place_instance` defaults to
  `None`. When `None`, friendly-name resolution is skipped — preserved
  for callers like the prefill auto-placement recursion that don't
  have a state handle, and for the test surface.
- `_select_drafter_placement` falls back to
  `model_card.drafter_eligible_nodes` when `resolved_eligible_nodes` is
  not provided, so any future internal caller that constructs the
  function call directly continues to behave correctly.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest src/exo/master/tests/test_placement_drafter_friendly_names.py` — 8 passed
- [x] `uv run pytest src/exo/master/tests/test_placement_drafter_asymmetric.py` — 22 passed (no regressions on existing asymmetric drafter coverage)
- [x] `uv run pytest src/exo/master/ src/exo/shared/` — 213 passed
- [x] `uv run pytest -x` — 1085 passed, 1 skipped (full repo sweep)
- [x] `uv run basedpyright src/exo/master/ src/exo/shared/models/` — 0 errors
- [x] `uv run ruff check` (touched files) — clean

## Operator workflow after this lands

Custom card overrides under `~/.exo/custom_model_cards/` can swap

```toml
drafter_eligible_nodes = ["12D3KooW...stale..."]
```

for

```toml
drafter_eligible_friendly_names = ["wc-bmbp"]
```

and the pin becomes portable across deployments + survives state wipes
automatically.

## Summary

Phase 10.26 — emit `Hotel.priceRange` in the parent hotel JSON-LD, derived from the rooms' editorial indicative prices (the columns shipped in #31).

`priceRange` is one of the few Google Hotels Rich Result fields the schema-dts builder already accepted (we just didn't have a number to put there). Wiring it gives the SERP card a coarse price anchor ("€950–€11 000") without requiring live ARI / Amadeus pricing — the fiche is in `display_only` mode and there is no concept of a real-time offer.

## Why

From the gap analysis (`docs/audits/peninsula-paris-gap-analysis.md` §2.15 row): `priceRange: ❌ — Pas de fourchette de prix (display_only)`. Now that Phase 10.23 added per-room `indicative_price_minor`, the hotel-level field is a thin derivation; emitting it closes one of the two remaining JSON-LD gaps from the audit. The other (`aggregateRating`) genuinely depends on a Google Places / Amadeus pipeline.

## Implementation

- **`computeHotelPriceRange(rooms, locale)`** added to `apps/web/src/lib/format-indicative-price.ts`:
  - Filters rooms that carry an editorial price.
  - Returns `null` on empty input — the page skips the JSON-LD field rather than emitting a misleading `€0` floor.
  - **Refuses to FX-convert**: if the priced rooms span more than one currency, returns `null`. Silent omission beats stale conversion. (This is a real edge case: aspirational dollar-anchored suites can co-exist with euro-anchored standard rooms.)
  - Picks `min(fromMinor)` and `max(toMinor ∥ fromMinor)`, formats both with `Intl.NumberFormat` (`maximumFractionDigits: 0`, fr-FR or en-GB).
  - Returns the single price when `min === max`, the range `"€950–€11 000"` otherwise.
- **Hotel page** (`apps/web/src/app/[locale]/hotel/[slug]/page.tsx`) calls the helper inside the existing `hotelInput` spread and forwards the field to `JsonLd.hotelJsonLd()` (already accepts `priceRange?: string`).
- **Vitest suite** added (`format-indicative-price.test.ts`, 11 cases) covering: locale-aware formatting fr-FR vs en-GB, missing `to`, no-fractional-digit guarantee, empty input, mixed-currency refusal, single-anchor reduction to a single string.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @cct/web test src/lib/format-indicative-price` — 11 / 11 passing.
- `pnpm --filter @cct/web typecheck` — clean.

## Files

- `apps/web/src/lib/format-indicative-price.ts` (+ 64 lines: new `computeHotelPriceRange` + `IndicativePriceMinor` re-export)
- `apps/web/src/lib/format-indicative-price.test.ts` (new, 11 cases, 108 lines)
- `apps/web/src/app/[locale]/hotel/[slug]/page.tsx` (+ 12 lines wiring the field into `hotelInput`)

## Skill / rule alignment

- `structured-data-schema-org` — Hotel.priceRange now present whenever rooms carry an editorial price; the rich-result coverage for Peninsula Paris moves from 22 / 24 to 23 / 24 fields against the audit checklist.
- `seo-technical` — the price anchor doubles as a localised AEO answer for *“combien coûte une nuit au Peninsula Paris ?”* without adding a FAQ entry.
- `typescript-strict` — no `as`, no `!`, discriminated by currency literal union; mixed-currency case handled by returning `null` rather than throwing.

Based on `feat/phase-10-25-room-subpage-polish` (#33). Merge after.

body:
## Summary

Adds a Download feature to the storage navigator that covers the three required scenarios — single file, multi-file, and select-all — through one server-side code path per scenario and zero new runtime dependencies.

## Design

**Single file.** The existing blob/file GET endpoints now honour `?download=1`, which sets `Content-Disposition: attachment` so the browser triggers Save As natively. The Electron embedded server also exposes a sibling `/api/download/...` route that does the same thing for the desktop UI.

**Multi-file.** New endpoint `POST /storages/:account/containers/:container/blobs:download-zip` (and a parallel one for file shares) takes `{ paths: string[], basePath?, archiveName? }` and streams a ZIP back. The stream uses `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` — no archive-wide buffering on the server. Each blob is opened lazily, drained into the response, then closed before the next one is opened, so memory stays bounded regardless of total archive size.

**"All files".** The UI does *not* introduce a second code path: the container right-click menu walks the listing (paginated, recursive) and feeds the collected paths into the same multi-file endpoint.

**Zip implementation.** New `API/src/streaming/zip-stream.ts` is a minimal STORE-mode (uncompressed) ZIP writer using Node 22's built-in `zlib.crc32` for incremental CRC computation. STORE mode lets bytes flow from Azure → ZIP frame → response without going through any compression buffer. No new npm dependencies. Limitations called out in the source: no Zip64 (entry size capped at 4 GiB, count at 65 535) — acceptable for the navigator UX, easy to revisit later if needed. A mirror copy lives at `src/util/zip-stream.ts` for the Electron embedded server because the API and client packages have separate `rootDir` boundaries.

**Auth.** All new API routes go through `requireRole('Reader')` — the existing RBAC chain. Nothing bypasses it.

**Archive layout.** `basePath` is stripped from each entry name before it's added to the archive, so "download this folder" produces a zip whose top-level matches what the user clicked on rather than the full container prefix.

## Tests

- `API/test/unit/zip-stream.test.ts` — 4 tests: CD validity, **lazy entry pulling** (verifies the second source is not opened until the first is drained), **chunked emit count** (asserts more than two distinct data events to prove the writer streams rather than buffers), `archiveName` path-traversal guard.
- `API/test/integration/blob-download.test.ts` — 3 tests against Azurite: `?download=1` produces `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="hello.txt"`; multi-file zip returns `application/zip` + `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + no `Content-Length`, central directory parsed and entry names + sizes verified; RBAC respected (Reader passes through).
- Full suite — Client: 181/181 pass. API: 91/91 pass (was 84, +7 new).

## Smoke run

`API/test_scripts/smoke-download.ts` boots Azurite + the app on a random port and hits the new endpoints over real HTTP. Output:

```
[smoke] GET single blob with ?download=1
  status=200 CT=text/plain CD=attachment; filename="one.txt"; filename*=UTF-8''one.txt
[smoke] POST blobs:download-zip (multi-file)
  status=200 CT=application/zip CD=attachment; filename="pack.zip" bytes=260 transfer=chunked
[smoke] wrote /tmp/smoke.zip
[smoke] OK — single download + streamed zip both work.
```

External validation with the system `unzip`:

```
$ unzip -l /tmp/smoke.zip
  Length      Date    Time    Name
       10  1980-01-01 00:00   one.txt
       16  1980-01-01 00:00   two.txt
         2 files

$ unzip -p /tmp/smoke.zip one.txt
first file
$ unzip -p /tmp/smoke.zip two.txt
second blob body
```

## UI surface

Three new context-menu items wired in `src/electron/public/app.js`:
- File right-click → **Download**
- Folder right-click → **Download as ZIP**
- Container right-click → **Download all as ZIP**

## Files

- `API/src/streaming/zip-stream.ts` (+`src/util/zip-stream.ts` mirror)
- `API/src/routes/{blobs,files}.ts` — new POST endpoints + `?download=1` on GET
- `src/electron/server.ts` — `/api/download` + `/api/download-zip` for both blobs and files
- `src/electron/public/{index.html,app.js}` — menu entries + handlers
- `API/test/unit/zip-stream.test.ts`, `API/test/integration/blob-download.test.ts`
- `API/test_scripts/smoke-download.ts`

## Test plan

author: arhaeem
body:
Closes #5 — Headed bootstrap reads cookies as anonymous despite successful login
Closes #6 — CLI symlink exit / shebang / keychain prompts / login persistence

---

## What changed

### Issue #5 — daemon anonymous mode after successful login

**Bug 1 (`fix/#5.1`)** — `PERPLEXITY_HEADLESS_ONLY=1` leaked from the launcher's IDE-config env block into the daemon's spawn env via `...process.env`. The daemon's `PerplexityClient.init()` then skipped the headed bootstrap entirely — the only phase that can solve CF challenges. Fixed by stripping `PERPLEXITY_HEADLESS_ONLY` and `PERPLEXITY_NO_DAEMON` from the spawn env in all three spawn sites (`daemon/launcher.ts`, `extension/src/daemon/runtime.ts`, `stdio-daemon-proxy.ts`).

**Bug 2 (`fix/#5.2`)** — Phase 2 (headless search) used `chromium.launch()` + ephemeral context. The fresh `cf_clearance` written to `browser-data/` by Phase 1 was never loaded. Phase 2 now uses `chromium.launchPersistentContext(browserData, ...)` — same directory as Phase 1, so the CF clearance is already on disk when Phase 2 starts. Vault cookies are injected selectively (only cookies not already on disk), so a freshly-written `cf_clearance` is never overwritten by a stale vault copy.

**Diagnostic gap (`fix/#5.3`)** — `getSavedCookies()` returned `[]` silently for four distinct failure modes. Now logs a specific message for each path: no `vault.enc`, `cookies` key absent, non-array value, JSON parse failure. An `unsealFailed` flag prevents the "key absent" message from firing when the real cause is an unseal error already logged by the catch path.

### Issue #6 — CLI/auth UX bugs (all four confirmed bugs)

**Bug 1 (`fix/#6.1`)** — CLI and daemon entrypoints silently exited 0 on symlinked invocations (npm global install, Homebrew Cellar, `node_modules/.bin/`). The `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` guard fails when `process.argv[1]` is a symlink. Extracted `isMainModule()` helper (`src/is-main-module.js`) that uses `realpathSync` on both sides, with a defensive fallback to the old comparison when `realpathSync` rejects.

**Bug 2 (`fix/#6.2`)** — `dist/cli.mjs` had no shebang or executable mode. tsup intentionally strips shebangs (they trip vitest/esbuild during test imports). New `scripts/post-build-shebang.mjs` post-build script prepends `#!/usr/bin/env node` and `chmod 755`s the file. No-op on Windows where npm uses `.cmd` wrappers.

**Bug 3 (`fix/#6.3`)** — Repeated macOS Keychain permission prompts from multiple `keytar.getPassword()` calls per session. `vault.js` now caches the keytar module reference in `_keytarModuleCache` (reset on `__resetKeyCache()`). `probeKeychainState()` is exported and shared across `cli.js` and `checks/vault.js`, removing three duplicate inline probe implementations. `PERPLEXITY_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN=1` escape hatch added for headless/CI environments.

**Bug 4 (`fix/#6.4`)** — Login runners (`login-runner.js`, `manual-login-runner.js`) used a non-persistent browser context, discarding Google SSO and Cloudflare state between login sessions. Now use `chromium.launchPersistentContext(paths.loginBrowserData, ...)` with a dedicated `login-browser-data/` directory (separate from the daemon's `browser-data/` to avoid Chromium singleton-lock collisions).

### Build fix

tsup's rollup-dts worker OOMs on this package's 47+ entry points under Node 22+. Build is now split: `tsup --no-dts` + `tsc --allowJs --emitDeclarationOnly` + post-build shebang script.

### Review polish (added during code review pass)

- `getSavedCookies`: `unsealFailed` flag prevents misleading double-log when vault unsealing throws
- Login runners: `ctx.browser()?.close()` (optional chain) so a null `browser()` return degrades gracefully

---

## Test coverage

- `test/is-main-module.test.js` — exact match, non-match, symlink, missing argv[1]
- `test/vault.test.js` — `probeKeychainState` caching + `PERPLEXITY_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN` escape hatch
- `test/config-getSavedCookies.test.js` — "no vault.enc" and "key absent" diagnostic log paths
- `extension/tests/transports/stdio-daemon-proxy.test.ts` — assert `PERPLEXITY_HEADLESS_ONLY` no longer injected
- `extension/tests/auto-config.test.ts` — same assertion for OpenCode transport

**130/130 test files pass. Full typecheck clean.**

---

## Smoke required before merge

Per `docs/release-process.md`: Win11 + macOS 14+ + Ubuntu 22+. Issue #6 bugs 1+2 specifically need the macOS row (Homebrew bin layout is the canonical symlink reproducer). Issue #5 bugs need the daemon-proxy transport path on any OS.

## Summary

Manual sweep of every plugin on a real wb7 controller (wirenboard-A25NDEMJ) surfaced three bugs in 0.3.0 that had escaped review, plus several gaps in the surface:

- **`rules disable/enable` were broken end-to-end** — wb-rules' Editor RPC rejects any save/rename whose target doesn't end in `.js`, so neither direction worked. Now done via plain `mv` (wb-rules notices via inotify), with explicit `RULES_NOT_FOUND` / `RULES_TARGET_EXISTS` so we never silently clobber the user's data.
- **`rules load`** returned the whole `{"content": ..., "enabled": ...}` envelope; the JSON source is now unwrapped.

- `wb_cli/lib/serial_conf.py` — shared parser for the serial config (consumed by both `modbus` and `modbus-fw`).

## What

Strip the 5-step progress card from `SpawnProgress` in `src/app/sessions/[sid]/view.tsx`. The creating-state card now just shows a spinner, an elapsed-time counter, and an honest hint about what to do if bring-up stalls.

The step list added by #34 (Creating sandbox / Pod scheduling / Image pull / boot / Harness ready / Cloning repo) advanced its highlighted step on elapsed-time thresholds, not on real backend phase data. The comment in the original code even called this out as "a lie" — a pod that's slow to schedule would look stuck on "Cloning repo" because the threshold fired before pod-scheduling actually finished.

In production this is worse than a frozen spinner. A user watching the card sees "Cloning repo" sit for minutes when the harness has been responsive and the repo cloned for a while. That's insulting.

Better to show nothing about phase than to show wrong info about phase.

- Pure UI cleanup. No backend, route, or type changes.

## Summary

Flip the liveness watchdog from alert-only to **alert + autoheal**. Single-line change to `deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service` ExecStart to add `--auto-restart-after 3`.

## Behavior change

Before:
- Heartbeat stale > 5 min → Telegram ping. That's it. Operator must SSH in and `systemctl restart ict-trader-live.service` manually.

After:
- Heartbeat stale > 5 min → Telegram ping.
- 3 consecutive stale checks (~8 min total stall) → watchdog runs `sudo -n systemctl restart ict-trader-live.service` + Telegrams the systemctl exit code.
- `last_autoheal_streak` gates re-fires so a persistently-broken trader doesn't restart-loop. The trader-side `Restart=always` (RestartSec=10) does the actual recovery work; this just kicks it.

## Why now

Watchdog has been firing cleanly on schedule since deploy of PR #950 — diag pull of `journalctl?unit=ict-liveness-watchdog.service` showed 16 consecutive fires `status=0` between 21:19Z and 21:36Z today. Alert path is known-trusted, so escalation to autoheal is the right next step. If the operator decides this is too aggressive after seeing it in action, reverting is a one-line strip of the CLI arg + redeploy.

## Test plan

- [x] Watchdog already proven to fire on 60 s cadence (issue #955 journal pull)
- [x] Autoheal logic already covered by 14 tests in `tests/test_heartbeat.py` from PR #950 — no code changes here

- [ ] (next time the trader actually stalls) confirm the autoheal Telegram lands

## Reverting

Strip `--auto-restart-after 3` from the ExecStart line and re-deploy. The watchdog falls back to alert-only.

author: guybedford
body:
This enables workerd to ship its `JsgLint` clang-tidy plugin against the workerd-tools-built clang-tidy binary.

Two coordinated changes:

* `build/llvm/common.args` flips `LLVM_ENABLE_PLUGINS=ON`, `CLANG_PLUGIN_SUPPORT=ON`, and adds `LLVM_ENABLE_RTTI=ON`. Without these the clang-tidy binary neither exports its symbols for `dlopen` resolution nor emits the typeinfo records that an out-of-tree plugin's vtable references, and `clang-tidy --load=...` fails.
* The LLVM workflow gains a packaging step that, when the requested target contains `clang-tidy`, builds a per-platform `llvm-<version>-<os>-clang-tidy-dev.tar.xz` asset. It contains the headers needed to compile an out-of-tree plugin against this exact build:

  ```
  clang/include/{clang,clang-c}/**
  llvm/include/{llvm,llvm-c}/**
  build/include/**                   # generated config headers
  build/tools/clang/include/**       # generated clang config headers
  clang-tools-extra/clang-tidy/**.h  # plugin API (only in the source tree)
  ```

  Layout mirrors the LLVM source tree, so a consumer just adds `-I clang/include -I llvm/include -I build/include -I build/tools/clang/include -I clang-tools-extra`. Generated headers under `build/` are platform-specific, hence one tarball per matrix entry.

The consuming workerd side (`build/tools/clang_tidy/plugin/BUILD.headers`) already expects this layout; once a release is cut with this workflow change, the temporary `new_local_repository` pointing at a hand-built LLVM tree gets replaced with a `github_release` entry in `build/deps/build_deps.jsonc`.

Verified the workflow's packaging step locally by mirroring it against a hand-built LLVM 22 source/build tree and confirming that `bazel build //build/tools/clang_tidy/plugin:JsgLint.so` in workerd consumes the resulting layout cleanly.

## Summary
- Bind `S-<insert>` to `ghostel-yank` in semi-char and readonly modes — the conventional alternative paste shortcut in browsers, terminal emulators, and file managers.
- Add `<remap> <yank>` to both maps so anything Emacs globally binds to `yank` (notably `s-v` on macOS, plus user rebinds) routes through `ghostel-yank` without a per-key entry. The darwin `s-v` special-case blocks in both maps are now redundant and removed.
- `C-y` stays explicitly bound so user rebinds of `yank`'s global key cannot break ghostel paste. Line mode keeps Emacs's regular `yank` (paste lands in the editable input region). Char mode is unchanged.

Closes #263.

## Why `S-<insert>` needs an explicit binding (not just the remap)
`ghostel--define-terminal-keys` iterates `<insert>` × `(S- C- M- C-S- M-S- C-M-)` and binds every combo to `ghostel--send-event`. That's a *direct* binding in `ghostel-semi-char-mode-map`, and direct bindings win over the `<remap>` chain — remap only fires on the command that the literal-key lookup resolves to. `s-v` flows through the remap fine because the helper's modifier list excludes super. Readonly mode never calls the helper, so the remap is enough there.

- [x] New ert: `ghostel-test-yank-remap-bindings` covers the `[remap yank]` entries in semi-char/readonly, the *absence* of the remap in line/char modes, char mode's `S-<insert>` still going to `ghostel--send-event`, and end-to-end `key-binding` resolution of `C-y`/`S-<insert>`/`s-v` (darwin) in an active ghostel buffer.

### What does this PR do?

The Task component in the session TUI route fires sync.session.sync(sessionId) as a fire-and-forget promise (void ...) without .catch(). body:
## Definitive root cause (4th iteration)

PR #30 was correct in mechanism but rested on a false assumption. The trace from the post-merge full-suite run is unambiguous:

\`\`\`
[4409ms] GET /health/live → TimeoutError (3000ms)
[7921ms] GET /health/live → TimeoutError (3000ms)
[11427ms] GET /health/live → TimeoutError (3000ms)
... (17 attempts, every single one timed out at exactly 3s) ...
[60497ms] GET /health/live → TimeoutError (3000ms)
[61192ms] hook@2 beforeEach → Test timeout of 60000ms exceeded
\`\`\`

The backend NEVER woke during the 60s test budget. Render free-tier deep-cold spin-up is regularly 60s+, sometimes longer. **No per-test budget can absorb that.** The warm-up has to run *outside* the test loop.

## Fix
\`e2e/global-setup.ts\` runs **once before any test**, polling \`/health/live\` with a **5-minute budget** and 4s per-request timeout. After it returns, every test's \`waitForBackend\` probe finds a warm backend and resolves in <500 ms.

No-op when \`BACKEND_HEALTH_URL\` is unset — local sqlite runs against the playwright \`webServer\` and don't need a remote warm-up.

## Verified
- globalSetup completed in **0.3s on a warm backend** (one attempt, no overhead)
- All 5 \`admin-defect-types.spec.ts\` tests passed in 38.2s with \`--retries=0\`
- Will need a full-suite re-run after merge to confirm 182/182 — the real validation requires a deep-cold backend (≥15min idle) which I can't deterministically reproduce locally

## History (this PR closes it)
- PR #27: fixed hardcoded localhost:8000 + permissive assert — 1 fail, then 2 flaky
- PR #28: fixed textContent() data-race in floating-pool — defect-types still failed
- PR #29: fixed swallowed networkidle in defect-types nav helper — symptom, not cause
- PR #30: fixed waitForBackend per-request timeout — right code, wrong assumption
- **PR #31 (this one)**: actual root cause — pre-warm outside the test loop

Hover-revealed UI patterns create severe accessibility issues for keyboard-only users who navigate the interface using the `Tab` key, as they cannot trigger the mouse `hover` state. This change ensures these interactive elements become fully visible and clearly indicated when focused.

*Before:* Keyboard users tabbing through the UI would have hidden focus stops on action buttons (like Delete/Edit), with no visual indication that an interactive element existed or was currently focused.
*After:* When tabbing onto the action buttons, they become fully opaque and display a focus ring, allowing keyboard-only users to seamlessly discover and trigger these actions.
